original_test_intent: Verify BMC I2C-11 reaches both the temperature sensor and BMC FRU, returning a plausible sensor value and valid immutable FRU identity without disturbing thermal monitoring or EEPROM data.
original_method: Prove BMC I2C-11 maps to bus10; identify sensor0x48 and the separate FRU EEPROM endpoint; inspect driver ownership; read sensor temperature via supported interface or approved raw register0x00; decode signed/scaled two-byte value and correlate with BMC telemetry/reference; read only approved FRU header/identity bytes and validate signature/checksum; verify no alarms, thresholds or FRU content changed.
manual_activity: BMC/thermal/FRU owner supplies sensor and FRU maps, temperature decoder/tolerance, driver-safe access and EEPROM recovery policy; no physical probing is inferred.
required_inputs: PID1114953 mapping from BMC I2C-11 to Linux bus10, sensor0x48 and BMC FRU endpoint
Temperature-sensor part/revision and register0x00 format, endian, signedness, resolution and valid bits
Expected operating range and correlation tolerance to BMC hwmon/Redfish or independent reference
FRU address, safe header/identity offset/length and format/checksum oracle
Kernel hwmon/FRU driver ownership and approved supported interface or `-f` exception
safety_requirements: Do not run broad quick-write discovery on bus10
Prefer hwmon/driver reads; do not force0x48 while bound absent explicit approval
Confirm register0x00 read cannot clear alerts or change threshold/pointer state
Read FRU only at approved offsets/length; never write or dump arbitrary protected content
Abort on implausible temperature, alarm/monitoring loss, checksum failure, NACK, timeout, stuck bus or BMC degradation
agent_execution_scope: Collect bus/device identity, driver binding, sensor telemetry and FRU inventory baseline
After approval, read/decode/correlate temperature and separately validate bounded FRU identity/checksum
Do not probe/solder, scan blindly, change thresholds, write FRU, force bound devices by default, auto-retry or decide verdict
engineer_actions: Approve bus10 sensor and FRU endpoint map
Approve temperature decoder/range/tolerance and FRU read/checksum oracle
Approve driver-safe access or exceptional force, timeouts and recovery
Review distinct sensor/FRU evidence and issue verdict

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Incorrect physical-only substitution; source provides a remotely runnable sensor read.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Do not use broad `i2cdetect -q`. Prefer the bound hwmon interface; otherwise, after approval, retain `i2ctransfer -f -y 10 w1@0x48 0x00 r2`, decode/correlate the two bytes, and add a separate PID-defined read-only FRU header/identity/checksum check.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: BMC bus10, address0x48, register0x00, r2, BMC I2C-11, temperature sensor, BMC FRU, PID1114953 and 15/5-minute scope are preserved.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use driver-safe temperature telemetry plus a bounded raw/driver correlation and a separate immutable FRU identity/checksum read.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds measurable sensor accuracy/plausibility and missing FRU coverage while removing invented physical probing and unsafe broad scanning.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A two-byte response from sensor0x48 cannot prove BMC FRU connectivity; conversely, FRU presence does not validate temperature conversion or monitoring accuracy.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Forced reads can race thermal drivers; a single ambient reading tests plausibility/connectivity but not full sensor accuracy range; FRU evidence must avoid secrets and writes.

project_override_considerations: Wistron I2C policy requires BMC controller/bus and each target address/expected response. Thermal driver ownership and immutable FRU read boundaries are mandatory.
expected_evidence: PID topology for BMC I2C-11/bus10/sensor0x48/BMC FRU
Sensor/FRU part and firmware/data-format identity plus driver bindings
Vendor temperature register decoder and expected range/tolerance
Timestamped raw two bytes, decoded temperature and simultaneous independent telemetry comparison
Bounded FRU header/identity bytes with expected fields/checksum and no write
Pre/post thermal alarms, FRU integrity, bus/BMC health and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The source names both sensor and FRU but supplies only an un-decoded0x48 sensor read, no FRU address/content check and no expected temperature. Earlier reviews also impose physical probing absent from the Procedure.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Both read-only objectives are clear and require standard owner-supplied maps/decoders, so the correct classification is RPUC.

Define driver ownership and whether `-f` is allowed, safe scan policy, timeout/NACK/thermal-abort criteria and recovery; confirm physical probing is not mandatory unless separately scoped.

review_improvement: Restores remote functional automation, separates the sensor and FRU acceptance paths, and adds temperature decoding/correlation plus immutable FRU validation.
independent_technical_reasoning: The command addresses0x48 and returns two bytes, which can only support temperature-sensor evidence after a part-specific decoder. The title separately requires BMC FRU connectivity, for which no address or transaction is supplied. A complete review must therefore add a distinct bounded FRU identity/checksum read. The safety issue is driver and EEPROM integrity, not mandatory physical probing.
